\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Product Density}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.ProductDensity
\section{Overview}
Finite Gaussian products have the product of scalar densities and obey coordinatewise affine transformation laws. Coordinate moment formulas and density integration identities apply to these product laws.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Norm of a coordinate projection]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.norm_coordinateProjection_le_one}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For a finite set $I$ and $i\in I$, the coordinate projection $\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$, $x\mapsto x_i$, has operator norm at most one for the maximum norm.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Density of a finite Gaussian product]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.pi_gaussianReal_eq_withDensity}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be a finite set, $c\in\mathbb R^I$, $v>0$, and $\mu_{c,v}=\bigotimes_{i\in I}N(c_i,v)$. The measure $\mu_{c,v}$ has Lebesgue density $z\mapsto\prod_i p_v(c_i,z_i)$, where $p_v(c_i,z_i)$ is the scalar Gaussian density.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Integration against a Gaussian product density]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_pi_gaussianReal_eq_integral_smul}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.pi_gaussianReal_eq_withDensity}
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be a finite set, $c\in\mathbb R^I$, $v>0$, and $\mu_{c,v}=\bigotimes_{i\in I}N(c_i,v)$. For a real normed vector space $E$ and any $f:\mathbb R^I\to E$, $\int f\,d\mu_{c,v}=\int_{\mathbb R^I}(\prod_i p_v(c_i,z_i))f(z)\,dz$, where $p_v$ is the scalar Gaussian density and nonintegrable integrals on either side are assigned zero.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Affine finite Gaussian product law]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_gaussianAffine_pi}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be finite, $c\in\mathbb R^I$, and $s\in\mathbb R$. The map $y\mapsto(c_i+sy_i)_i$ pushes $\bigotimes_iN(0,1)$ to $\bigotimes_iN(c_i,s^2)$, including negative or zero $s$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Affine Gaussian density integration]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_affine_gaussian_pi_eq_density}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_pi_gaussianReal_eq_integral_smul,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_gaussianAffine_pi,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be finite, $c\in\mathbb R^I$, $s\ne0$, and $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ measurable. For a standard Gaussian vector $Y$, $\mathbb E f(c+sY)=\int_{\mathbb R^I}(\prod_i p_{s^2}(c_i,z_i))f(z)\,dz$, where $p_{s^2}$ is the scalar Gaussian density and nonintegrable integrals are assigned zero.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Integrability of a centered coordinate square]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_centered_sq_gaussianCoordinate}
\leanok
\difficulty{1}
For a finite set $I$, $c\in\mathbb R^I$, $v\ge0$, and $i\in I$, the function $z\mapsto(z_i-c_i)^2$ is integrable under $\bigotimes_jN(c_j,v)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Centered second coordinate moment]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_centered_sq_gaussianCoordinate}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_centered_sq_gaussianReal}
\difficulty{4}
For a finite set $I$, $c\in\mathbb R^I$, $v\ge0$, and $i\in I$, $\int(z_i-c_i)^2\,d(\bigotimes_jN(c_j,v))(z)=v$.
\end{lemma}
